clue.text: Shady types dressed up in denim mode?

indicators.note: dressing something up disguises it, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion question: are these louche characters showing off a denim look?
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed up' rearranges the letters of DENIM MODE. The question mark admits the surface is a pun on fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: The demi-monde is a fringe social world of disreputable people, kept women and their hangers-on.

clue.text: Passed on rhythm for one tramping

parts.note: to pass on is to die, so passed on means dead
a beat is a rhythm in music

explanation.surface: A dead rhythm that suits a marching walker.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadbeat is a down-and-out idler, a tramp or vagrant.

clue.text: Damp vapour conceals nothing

indicators.note: conceals means the word for vapour hides another letter inside

parts.note: mist is fine water vapour in the air
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Wet air that hides nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conceals' puts O inside MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly wet, as damp is.

clue.text: Sacred peak? SOS — a man turns up drunk here!

indicators.note: drunk means reeling and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A distress call: a man staggers up a holy mountain, drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' looks like a reversal sign but is fodder; 'drunk' rearranges SOS A MAN TURNS UP. Parnassus is the Greek mountain sacred to Apollo and the Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek mountain was holy to Apollo and the Muses, a home of poetry.

clue.text: Part of finger fixed round book

indicators.note: round means the word for fixed goes around another letter

parts.note: nailed means fixed in place

explanation.surface: A fingertip area fastened round a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts NAILED around B.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft tissue under the fingernail is one part of a finger.

clue.text: Traveller entering European city upset ruler

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read bottom to top
entering means the traveller goes inside the city

parts.note: Rome is a European city
a rep, a sales representative, is a commercial traveller

explanation.surface: A salesman arriving in a European capital unsettles its leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' builds ROREPME; 'upset' in a down clue turns it upside down. A rep is a salesman, a commercial traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor rules an empire as its sovereign.

clue.text: Early chieftain not working with Angles, initially

parts.note: a machine that is off is not working

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word Angles

explanation.surface: A tribal leader of old who is idle, alongside the Angles.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the English Midlands; he built the earthwork Offa's Dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa was an Anglo-Saxon ruler, a king of Mercia in the eighth century.

clue.text: Meal? Donkey tucks into fine grain with energy

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: tucks into means the donkey goes inside the word for grain

parts.note: rice is a cereal grain
an ass is a donkey
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Dinner time: a donkey eats fine grain with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' looks like a donkey eating, but it is the container signal; 'Meal?' with its question mark is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A fricassee is a dish of stewed meat in a white sauce.

clue.text: Reluctant to state limits of statute

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

indicators.note: limits of asks for the first and last letters of statute

explanation.surface: Unwilling to declare the boundaries of a law.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means being opposed or disinclined to it.

clue.text: Watches for breaking stories undeviatingly

indicators.note: breaking means the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: lies are stories, untruths

explanation.surface: Someone on the lookout for breaking news stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking stories' reads as news, but 'breaking' rearranges WATCHES FOR together with LIES, the word for 'stories'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in a straight line, by the most direct route.

clue.text: Farewell announcement that is presented by Unionist

parts.note: an ad is an announcement in a newspaper
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A goodbye notice put out by a Unionist politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A French word of parting used in English to mean goodbye.

clue.text: One, huge, absorbs first of punches without expression

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: absorbs means the word for huge takes another letter into itself

parts.note: huge means massive

indicators.note: first of asks for the opening letter of punches

explanation.surface: A huge boxer soaks up blows while keeping a straight face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbs' puts P, the first letter of 'punches', inside MASSIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An impassive face shows no emotion, a deadpan look.

clue.text: Place for washing sporting equipment, taking time in the middle

parts.note: a bat is equipment for cricket or baseball

indicators.note: taking means the word for middle takes in the letter for time

parts.note: the hub is the centre or middle of something

explanation.surface: Somewhere to clean sports kit, with a time slot in the middle of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the middle' is not a position indicator but a synonym; 'taking' makes it swallow the letter for time.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath is a tub filled with water in which one washes.

clue.text: Brings warmth to the ears afresh

indicators.note: afresh means anew, so the letters of the words are arranged again

explanation.surface: Something warms your ears all over again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afresh' rearranges THE EARS; 'Brings warmth to' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To warm food up again is to bring it back up to temperature.

clue.text: Superior attitude in broadcasts with good contests

parts.note: a programme that airs is broadcast
and means with, joining things
races are contests of speed

explanation.surface: A haughty air shown in radio programmes featuring fine competitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on affected manners to seem grander than others is a snobbish pose.

clue.text: What will echo list curious person picked up?

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means lifted, so the run of letters reads upwards

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties
a noser is a nosy, curious person

explanation.surface: A question about who repeats things: an inquisitive person overhears a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' wants to be a sound signal, but in a down clue it turns ROTANOSER (ROTA and NOSER) to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonator is a body that vibrates in sympathy, reinforcing and prolonging sound.

clue.text: Dancing skater is a star

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dancing skater is the star of the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing' rearranges SKATER IS; 'a star' is the definition, not praise.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed symbol * is shaped like a little star, from the Greek for small star.

clue.text: Novel implication of incest?

explanation.surface: A book title that hints at a forbidden family relationship.
explanation.definitionFit: D. H. Lawrence wrote this novel; read literally its title pairs sons with lovers, suggesting incest.

clue.text: Rodrigo's farewell, penning a grand few pieces

indicators.note: penning means the farewell shuts the other letters in

parts.note: Rodrigo stands for a Spanish speaker, whose goodbye is adios
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A composer's goodbye encloses a few grand musical pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' puts A and G inside ADIOS. Joaquin Rodrigo was a Spanish composer, famous for the Adagio of his Concierto de Aranjuez.
explanation.definitionFit: Slow movements in music are named for the tempo marking, so several such movements make a plural.

clue.text: Split up hellish cult?

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and his realm, so hellish suggests it
a sect is a cult

explanation.surface: Break up a devilish religious group?
explanation.definitionFit: To dissect is to cut apart for examination.

clue.text: Greek character embraced by former Catholic

indicators.note: embraced by means the Greek letter goes inside the word for former

parts.note: past means former, bygone
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person hugged by an ex-Catholic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catholic' alone is the definition; 'former' belongs to the wordplay, and 'embraced by' is the container signal. Papist is a derogatory term.
explanation.definitionFit: Papist is a hostile name for a Roman Catholic, a follower of the Pope.

clue.text: Failure to identify first-rate ballad one recalled

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the whole run of letters is turned backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as A and I
a ballad is a song
a means one

explanation.surface: Forgetting a top-class ballad when trying to bring it to mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns the whole of AISONGA backwards. A1, the first-rate mark, is written with the letter I for the figure 1.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical term for the brain's inability to recognise objects, people or sounds.

clue.text: Almost put up with receiving one Conservative answer

indicators.note: receiving means the shortened word takes the other letters inside it
almost means the word for put up with loses its last letter

parts.note: to suffer something is to put up with it
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Nearly tolerated taking on a Tory reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts SUFFER to SUFFE, which 'receiving' opens to take in IC. 'Answer' is the verb, as in 'that will answer the purpose'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be adequate for a need, or serve the purpose, is a verb sense of answer.

clue.text: Say friend in France turned up picture

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the letters read upwards

parts.note: e.g., for example, means say
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: Perhaps a French friend found a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reads EG and AMI upwards, giving the whole run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a likeness or picture.

clue.text: Disrupting most of University is causing annoyance

indicators.note: disrupting throws into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
most of means the word University loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Interfering with most of the university is a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the Y of UNIVERSITY; 'Disrupting' rearranges the remaining UNIVERSIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prying or obtrusive bothers people by intruding where it is not wanted.

clue.text: Arab with two receiving King, Ace and Queen

indicators.note: receiving means the letters for two take the others inside

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king
A is the card abbreviation for ace
Q is the card abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A card player holding a pair is dealt king, ace and queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts RAQ between the two letters I of II.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Baghdad's country is an Arab of that nation.

clue.text: Part of year occurring in the later months

indicators.note: occurring in tells us the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A season that falls in the later months of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occurring in' points to the letters running across 'laTER Months'.
explanation.definitionFit: A school or university year is divided into terms, such as the autumn term.

clue.text: Boozer ready to swallow water containing a drop of Pernod, in other words

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard, a boozer

indicators.note: to swallow means the word for ready takes the rest inside it

parts.note: OK means all set, ready

indicators.note: containing means the word for water holds a letter inside

parts.note: the sea is water

indicators.note: a drop of asks for just the first letter of Pernod

explanation.surface: A drinker happy to down water with a splash of aniseed spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a drop of' takes one letter of Pernod, a French aniseed drink; 'containing' and 'to swallow' nest the pieces in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase used to show an expression is figurative, roughly meaning 'as it were'.
